title: Stack the blockers
question: Blocks aren't declared yet. That 6/6 is the problem — can you kill it this combat, and how do you set your blocking formation?
solution:
**Yes. Put both Robots in one column, in front of theirs.** The 6/6 dies.

The rule that a column deals **combined power** isn't just an attacking rule — **a defending column sums too**. So:

- One Robot blocking alone deals **3**. The 6/6 shrugs it off.
- **Both Robots stacked in the same column** (one front, one back) deal **3 + 3 = 6** — exactly enough to kill a 6/6.

Damage into their column runs front to back, so all 6 lands on Generic Unit 6/6 and kills it. There's **no excess**, so the Robot 3 behind it walks away untouched.

What it costs you: their column deals **9** (6 + 3) into your blocking column. Your front Robot (3/3) takes 3 and dies, and the **6 excess carries to the back Robot** (3/3), which dies too. So you trade **both 3/3s for their 6/6** and take **0** damage.

Your Generic Unit 2/2 stays out of it — a column is only ever **two deep**, so it can't join the stack, and throwing it in front of nothing achieves nothing.
hints: One 3/3 in front of that column doesn't do much. What if two of them were in the same column?
A DEFENDING column deals combined power too — the rule cuts both ways.
notes: Everything on this board is a token, so there's no card text anywhere — it really is just the numbers. Your three units are in play but not yet in formation.
author: Bena
